land.text: Venetia from Lake Garda to the Tagliamento: Ateste, Patavium, Vicetia

capitals.name: Ateste (Este)
capitals.note: The Este culture's type site; no capital on the page (confidence 1).

correction.text: 'The Veneti were initially attested in the area between Lake Garda and the Euganean Hills'; western border along Lake Garda, southern 'from the Tartaro river... follows the Po and reaches Adria', eastern 'up to the Tagliamento river'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Veneti row. The page has no infobox area. Venetia is the Veneto east of Garda to the Tagliamento; Aquileia and the Friulian plain beyond the Tagliamento are not drawn (the page's eastern limit is the Tagliamento). Soft edges.

correction.text: Venetia without Verona: the Cenomani 'eventually absorbed the areas of Brescia and Verona' (Adriatic Veneti page); 'Verona also lay within their territory' (Cenomani page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from the Celtic settlement of the Po plain the Cenomani hold Verona (cenomani dossier, -400..-89, which the Veneti page confirms with 'eventually absorbed the areas of Brescia and Verona'); the Veneti keep Venetia east of the Adige. The year -400 is the cenomani dossier's placeholder.

correction.text: Venetia without Verona: the Cenomani 'eventually absorbed the areas of Brescia and Verona' (Adriatic Veneti page); 'Verona also lay within their territory' (Cenomani page); ally of Rome since c. 238

keyframe_review.note: Same shape as -400..-239; from c. 238 the Veneti are friends and allies of Rome ('amicitia with Rome against the Gauls c. 238 BC'), so the renderer tints the land as a Roman client (vassal_start 238, vassal_end 89, matching the roman-republic dossier). Latin rights followed in 89.

region.text: Venetia from Lake Garda to the Tagliamento: Ateste, Patavium, Vicetia

ledger.note: c. 900 BC: Este I (c. 900-750 BCE), 'when the Veneti settle the Po Valley'; 'initially attested in the area between Lake Garda and the Euganean Hills', later 'borders similar to today's Veneto': Lake Garda, the Tartaro and Po to Adria, the Tagliamento. Cities Ateste, Patavium, Vicetia, Opitergium.

region.text: Verona, which the Cenomani hold; the Veneti keep Venetia to the east

ledger.note: c. 400 BC: the Celtic Cenomani settle the Po plain west of the Veneti and 'eventually absorbed the areas of Brescia and Verona'; the page gives no year, so -400 is the cenomani dossier's placeholder (the cenomani found event names 'nobody').

region.text: Venetia without Verona: the Cenomani 'eventually absorbed the areas of Brescia and Verona' (Adriatic Veneti page); 'Verona also lay within their territory' (Cenomani page)

ledger.note: c. 238 BC: the Veneti 'established amicitia with Rome against the Gauls'; friendship and alliance rather than subjection, so the tint is light.

region.text: Venetia without Verona: the Cenomani 'eventually absorbed the areas of Brescia and Verona' (Adriatic Veneti page); 'Verona also lay within their territory' (Cenomani page)

ledger.note: 89 BC: the Lex Pompeia de Transpadanis, 'promulgated by the Roman Consul Pompeius Strabo in 89 BC', gives Latin rights to the communities of Transpadana; the Veneti page puts the Veneti among them ('given Latin rights after the Social War in the Lex Pompeia de Transpadanis').

region.text: Venetia without Verona: the Cenomani 'eventually absorbed the areas of Brescia and Verona' (Adriatic Veneti page); 'Verona also lay within their territory' (Cenomani page)

ledger.note: 89 BC: Latin rights; the Venetic communities become Latin towns, then Roman citizens with the Lex Roscia (49 BC) and Regio X Venetia et Histria under Augustus (Adriatic Veneti page).

certainty.note: Venetia between Lake Garda, the Po and the Tagliamento; Verona goes to the Cenomani from c. 400 (placeholder); the Adige line is soft.

notes: New state. Venetia from Este I (c. 900) to the lex Pompeia (89, month 12 to match the roman-republic vassal_end).
